newsitem.title: USA: Fed's Yellen sees U.S. demand growth moderating.
newsitem.headline: Fed's Yellen sees U.S. demand growth moderating.

text.p: Federal Reserve Governor Janet Yellen said Thursday that she saw U.S. demand growth moderating for the remainder of 1996 and into 1997.
Yellen made her comments at the Joint Board of Directors meeting for the Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City.
"Forecasters say the recent pace of demand growth is likely to soon moderate toward a sustainable pace," she said.
"Personally, I consider such a prediction sensible and most probable, given my own perceptions of fundamentals driving key components of demand at this stage of the expansion," she said.

"Turning toward the fundamental factors that drive consumption and investment decisions, I find it hard to identify any balance that would be likely to spur unsustainably rapid growth on a longer term basis," she said.
Yellen also said the Fed's goal of price stability had not yet been reached, but said, "We are getting close."
She added that she felt the U.S. economy was probably "just one business cycle away from price stability."
Yellen said it was "too soon to tell for sure whether wage pressures presented too much of an upside risk to the economy."

"At a minimum, the fact that compensation (pressure) has been so far contained ... has made it easier for the Fed to keep inflation under control. If this trend continues, it may be possible to make inroads on inflation while operating with labor market conditions that historically have been associated with a less favorable inflation outlook," she said.
